title: The Protocol of the Free Port
premise: Freya Yarrow, a hostage negotiator haunted by the one call she couldn't save, works a quiet desk at a Baltic free port until a cargo flight's records are erased mid-flight—along with everyone who signed its manifest. The vanished plane carries Marek Voss, a defector holding a ledger of the port's owners, and Freya is ordered to extract him before the border checkpoint shifts change at dawn. As she follows rules that keep being rewritten to bury her, she discovers the erasure was authorized by her own mentor, and that her five years of invisibility were someone else's design. In the end Freya trades herself as collateral to walk Voss across the border, exposes the ledger at cost of her career, and finds that the found family of misfits who helped her—the dispatcher, the forger, the young guard—are the inheritance worth more than anything written in it.
about_author: Silas Galloway is the pen name of a former maritime logistics analyst who spent a decade inside bonded free ports before walking away. He writes thrillers about paper trails and the people they erase.

chapters.title: The Quiet Desk
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Five years after the Halvard failure, she negotiates a routine dockworker standoff at the Baltic free port with flawless restraint, then goes home alone to a flat with no photographs. Emotional beat: controlled numbness, the discipline of staying small.

chapters.title: Flight 4471
chapters.summary: Dispatcher Ilse's POV. A cargo flight files normally, then every record—flight plan, manifest, crew list—vanishes while the transponder still blips. Ilse calls Freya because Freya once bought her coffee during an audit. Beat: first crack in the routine, dread dressed as paperwork.

chapters.title: Rules That Rewrite Themselves
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. She pulls the file and finds it reclassified under her own authorization code—a code she never used. Her supervisor, Anselm Roth, gently suggests she let it go. Beat: gaslit unease; the board is being reset around her.

chapters.title: The Man Who Wasn't on the Manifest
chapters.summary: Marek Voss's POV. Hiding in a maintenance hangar, the defector catalogs what he knows: the ledger naming the port's true owners, including names Freya would recognize. He needs a negotiator, not a smuggler. Beat: wary hope; two invisible people orbiting the same hole.

chapters.title: Checkpoint Shifts
chapters.summary: Young border guard Tomas's POV. Tomas maps the shift changes he's not supposed to notice: a ninety-minute window at 04:10 when the east gate runs skeleton crew. He doesn't know yet why he'll need it. Beat: innocence arming itself.

chapters.title: The Forger's Terms
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. She seeks out Denny Kask, a disgraced documents man living above a sauna, who agrees to build Voss new papers—for a price: the truth of what happened to his brother, erased from the same system years ago. Beat: found family begins assembling, transactional but warm.

chapters.title: One Failure Still on the Board
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Freya's POV. The Halvard negotiation: the bus, the eleven hours, the shot she still hears. Roth was there too, and made a call she's never questioned—until now. Beat: grief reframed; the past is evidence.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Names
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Voss shows Freya a photograph of one ledger page: her mentor's signature beside a shell company that owns the port's cold storage—and the flight that never happened. Beat: betrayal's cold arrival; trust becomes a liability.

chapters.title: Ilse Disappears
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Dispatcher Ilse misses her shift; her apartment is professionally empty, her employment record now shows she never worked there. The erasure machine has started eating people. Beat: fear going public; stakes turn mortal.

chapters.title: The Offer You Can't Refuse Politely
chapters.summary: Roth's POV. Roth offers Freya a promotion, a transfer, a clean slate—if she delivers Voss to 'custody' off-book. He frames it as protection. She hears a leash. Beat: temptation and clarity in the same breath.

chapters.title: Ninety Minutes
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Planning montage: Denny's papers, Tomas's window, Ilse's hidden backup drive recovered from a locker. They rehearse the extraction like a negotiation—because that's what it is: getting a hostile party to say yes. Beat: purpose replacing paralysis.

chapters.title: Cold Storage
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Voss retrieves the full ledger from the cold storage vault, tripping a silent alarm he didn't know existed. Now the clock isn't dawn—it's minutes. Beat: adrenaline, guilt at endangering his rescuers.

chapters.title: The Hangar Standoff
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Port security corners them in the hangar. Freya does what she does best: talks. Eleven hours of skill compressed into twenty minutes as she negotiates a corridor out using their own rules against them. Beat: mastery under fire; the failure finally answering back.

chapters.title: Tomas's Choice
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. At the east gate, Tomas must wave through a car he knows is a lie—or refuse and become complicit in something worse. He opens the barrier. Beat: coming of age; innocence spent deliberately.

chapters.title: Dawn Interception
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Two kilometers from the border, a black car forces them off the road. Roth steps out—not with police, but with the men who own the checkpoint. Beat: trap sprung; the state was never the adversary, only its costume.

chapters.title: The Negotiation
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Freya negotiates with Roth directly: Voss and the ledger for herself—her silence, her record, her surrender. Roth, who taught her everything, accepts, revealing he erased Flight 4471 to protect the Halvard cover-up's paymasters. Beat: sacrifice as strategy; mentor and student finally speaking honestly.

chapters.title: Bait Before the Shift Change
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Held in a port office, Voss realizes Freya planned even this: the ledger page Roth 'confiscated' is Denny's forgery, seeded with a tracker. Beat: reversal; the bait was double-hooked.

Multiple POVs interwoven. During the skeleton-crew window, Tomas walks Voss out; Denny's tracker leads an international fraud unit to the port; Ilse, alive and hiding, transmits the real ledger to three newspapers simultaneously. Beat: convergence; every small loyalty cashing in at once.

chapters.title: What Freya Gave Up
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. In custody, stripped of clearance, Freya watches the news report the arrests without her name in them—Roth took her deal seriously, and so did the journalists. Beat: hollow victory; the cost itemized.

chapters.title: The Ledger's Last Page
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Voss reveals the final page he kept back: Halvard wasn't random—it was a test of Roth's methods, and Freya was chosen afterward to be shaped into exactly what Roth needed. Her failure had authors. Beat: rage transmuted into release; blame redistributed.

chapters.title: Inheritance
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Months later: no badge, no clearance, but a small consultancy run from Denny's sauna building—Ilse dispatching, Tomas studying law, Voss writing testimony. Freya takes a call from a stranger whose records just vanished. Beat: warmth earned; the family is the estate.

chapters.title: The Protocol of the Free Port
chapters.summary: Freya's POV, closing. She drives to the coast where the erased flight's wreckage was quietly buried, reads the eleven Halvard names aloud, and leaves the forged ledger page as a marker. Some protocols exist to be broken by the right person. Beat: mourning completed; the board finally cleared.
